title: Equivalence Theorem for Covering Data
body_html:
Equivalence Theorem for Covering Data

Let \(\widetilde\Sigma\) and \(\widetilde\Sigma'\) be covering supercuspidal data. Then \[ \widetilde\pi_{\widetilde\Sigma}\simeq \widetilde\pi_{\widetilde\Sigma'} \] if and only if \(\widetilde\Sigma\) and \(\widetilde\Sigma'\) are equivalent.
proof_html:
Equivalence of data immediately identifies the genuine \(K\)-types after conjugacy, so the compact inductions are isomorphic.

Conversely, Mackey theory gives a nonzero summand \[ \operatorname{Hom}_{\widetilde K\cap g\widetilde K'\!g^{-1}} (\widetilde\eta_{\widetilde\Sigma}, g\widetilde\eta_{\widetilde\Sigma'}) \] for some \(g\). Since the canonical splittings agree on the pro-unipotent intersection, the positive-depth part reduces to the weak-symmetry criterion of Hakim-Murnaghan. After conjugating, one may align \(\Gamma\) and \(\Gamma'\), hence \(G^0=G'^0\). Lemma 3.9 supplies a common depth character on \(G^0\), reducing the remaining comparison to depth zero. Howard-Weissman's depth-zero result gives a conjugacy \(g\in G^0\) matching the finite reductive quotient representations, and the only extra term is the splitting-difference character \(\mu_{\xi',\xi^g}\). This is exactly Definition 3.16.
